- Orange (20 pixels) at (16, 40) - unchanged!

- Dark gray (12 pixels) at (18, 57) - white position became dark gray
So clicking on the orange at (16, 40) consumed the white at (18, 57) without moving the orange. The orange stayed at (16, 40).
This is different from before when clicking on the orange moved it. The difference is that the white was at (18, 57), not adjacent to the orange.
Previously, when the white was at (21, 8) and I clicked on the orange at (17, 30), the orange moved. But now, when the white is at (18, 57) and I click on the orange at (16, 40), the orange doesn't move.
Wait, let me re-examine. Earlier:
1. White at (18, 57), orange at (17, 30) -> click orange -> orange moved to (17, 21), white to (17, 30)
2. White at (17, 30), orange at (17, 21) -> click orange -> orange moved to (17, 17), white to (17, 21)
3. White at (17, 21), orange at (17, 17) -> click orange -> white disappeared, orange stayed at (17, 17)
4. White at (21, 8), orange at (17, 30) -> click orange -> orange moved to (16, 38), white to (17, 30)
5. White at (17, 30), orange at (16, 38) -> click orange -> orange moved to (16, 40), white disappeared
6. White at (18, 57), orange at (16, 40) -> click orange -> white disappeared, orange stayed at (16, 40)
So the orange only moves when the white is on the path (adjacent to the orange or on the trail). When the white is at (18, 57), which is not on the path, clicking on the orange just consumes the white.
This means I need to get the white onto the path first, and then click on the orange to move it.
The path consists of the light gray trail pixels. Let me check where the trail is.
Looking at the objects:
- w(6) at (15, 33)
- w(8) at (17, 48)
These are the light gray trail pixels. The white needs to be on one of these positions to activate the orange's movement.
But the white only moves to dark gray diamond positions or follows the orange. It doesn't move to trail positions.
Wait, let me re-examine. When the white was at (18, 57) and I clicked on the orange at (17, 30), the white moved to (17, 30), which is the orange's position. So the white moves to the orange's position when I click on the orange.
But now, when the white is at (18, 57) and I click on the orange at (16, 40), the white disappears instead of moving to (16, 40).
The difference might be the distance. When the white was at (18, 57) and the orange was at (17, 30), they were closer (distance ~38 columns). Now, the white is at (18, 57) and the orange is at (16, 40), they are also close (distance ~20 columns).
Hmm, but the orange moved from (17, 30) to (16, 40) through several steps. Maybe the orange is now "stuck" at (16, 40) and can't move further.
Let me try a different approach. Let me move the white to the dark gray at (14, 27), which is on the path near the orange. Then click on the orange to see if it moves.

# Let me move white to dark gray at (14, 27), which is near the orange at (16, 40).
# First respawn white at (18, 57).

result = action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 18, 'col': 57}])
print(f"Respawned: level_completed={result.get('level_completed', False)}")

# Now move white to dark gray at (14, 27)
result2 = action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 14, 'col': 27}])
print(f"Moved to (14, 27): level_completed={result2.get('level_completed', False)}")

seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
print("\nObjects after:")
for n in sorted(nodes, key=lambda x: min(b[0] for b in x['boundary'])):
    if 5 <= n['pixels'] < 100:
        center = (sum(b[0] for b in n['boundary'])//len(n['boundary']), sum(b[1] for b in n['boundary'])//len(n['boundary']))
        print(f"  color={n['color']}, pixels={n['pixels']}, center~{center}")

# Check adjacency of white
adj = seg['adjacency_list']
white_id = None
for i, n in enumerate(nodes):
    if n['color'] == 'W' and n['pixels'] == 12:
        white_id = i
        break
if white_id is not None:
    print(f"\nWhite adjacent to:")
    for a, b in adj:
        if a == white_id or b == white_id:
            other = b if a == white_id else a
            print(f"  {nodes[other]['color']}({nodes[other]['pixels']})")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
